newsitem.title: UK: Copper perks up on LME, but others end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Copper perks up on LME, but others end mixed.

text.p: Copper prices pushed higher during Tuesday afternoon LME trading to challenge the upper end of a new chart band, but other metals lacked appetite, closing mixed.

Traders said copper again dominated activity with wide price movements seen as the market geared up for Wednesday's September option declarations. A brief spell of consolidation in mid-afternoon was ended by a flurry of covering, although solid resistance at $2,050 choked this off.
"It (copper) is in a new range now. There is key support at $1,970 - the break-out point - and resistance at $2,045/2,050. We've tested both of those today," one trader said.
Although the overall trend in the spreads was softer today, the cash/threes backwardation widened from midsession levels near $20 to stand at $26/29 at the close.

Traders said nearby tightness has all but been eradicated, with cash to next week's September date now showing a minimal $1 backwardation, as many September shorts have either rolled forward into October or closed out.
Last three months business was at $2,040 a tonne, up $14 from Monday's kerb close.

Movements were less extreme in the rest of the complex, with aluminium mostly content to hold above $1,500. Traders expect the market to stay within a broader $1,470/1,530 band, with last kerb trade today at $1,505, a $5 loss.
Nickel prices flipped higher during the afternoon rings, with buy-stops above $7,500 carrying the market up to $7,600 at one point before last trade at $7,550, a $135 gain from Monday.

Traders said the market is still trying to consolidate after recent wide price moves, with some support expected around today's low of $7,400. However, thin conditions mean price movements will remain volatile.
Lead attempted to push higher this afternoon, but faltered at the $820 level. However, prices still closed with modest gains with final business at $819, up $4.
The zinc market hardly budged from Monday levels, fluctuating aimlessly in a narrow band with last trade at $1,033, down $2 from yesterday's kerb close.
Tin also stayed close to previous closing levels, concluding the kerb at $6,250 against Monday's $6,250/6,260. The alloy market was indicated at a slightly softer $1,290/1,295 a tonne.
